resources.string:
SpoofNet records how well your phone receives satellite navigation signals (GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou and others), so that jamming and spoofing can be studied.

What is collected: raw satellite measurements (signal strength, timing, receiver gain), the satellites in view, the position reported by GPS and by the mobile network, motion sensor readings, and battery level.

Where it goes: the raw data stays on this phone, in a file that only this app can write. Nothing is uploaded. This version of the app has no internet permission at all. A file leaves the phone only if you export it yourself with the share button.

Listening only: the app only listens to signals that are already there. It never transmits anything and never asks your phone to transmit. Transmitting on satellite navigation frequencies is illegal almost everywhere, and no SpoofNet test needs it.

The app does not point you towards any source of interference and does not reward getting closer to one. Please do not go looking for interference.

Your responsibility: in some countries, recording interference near military or other defence sites may be restricted. You are responsible for following the law where you use the app.
